text.title: Rails ActiveRecord Examples
text.summary: Worked example: hardening an Order model with named scopes, boundary eager-loading, an enum status, transactional multi-writes and timezone-safe time calls.

example.context: Rails 7 commerce app. `Order#status` is a free-text column; `OrdersController#index` iterates `Order.all` and reads `o.customer.name`; the create path writes the order and decrements inventory in two unrelated statements; `Time.now` appears twelve times.
example.walk: Step 1: extract the repeated filters into `scope :recent` and `scope :paid`. Step 2: the index becomes `Order.includes(:customer, :items).recent`, eager-loaded at the controller boundary. Step 3: a migration turns `status` into an integer and the model declares `enum status: { pending: 0, paid: 1, shipped: 2, cancelled: 3 }`, so queries become `Order.pending` and `order.paid?`. Step 4: the create path wraps both writes in `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction`. Step 5: `counter_cache: true` on `OrderItem#belongs_to :order` plus an `items_count` column removes the per-row `COUNT(*)` on the index. Step 6: the `Rails/TimeZone` cop is enabled and all twelve `Time.now` calls become `Time.current`.
example.output: The index drops from 51 queries to 3; a status typo can no longer reach the database; the multi-write path is atomic; timestamps agree with `config.time_zone`.

example.note: Named scopes instead of duplicated `where`, an enum instead of magic strings, one transaction around the two writes, and `Time.current` rather than `Time.now`.
